name: Achaia
description: The heart of ancient Greece, home to Athens, Corinth, and Sparta, where philosophy, democracy, and early Christianity flourished.

name: Aegyptus
description: Land of the Pharaohs and the Nile, where Alexandria became a center of learning and early Christian thought.

name: Aethiopia
description: Ancient kingdom south of Egypt, known in Biblical times as a land of mystery and wealth, often associated with the Queen of Sheba.

name: Arabia Deserta
description: The vast desert interior of Arabia, home to nomadic tribes and ancient trade routes connecting the Near East.

name: Arabia Felix
description: The fertile 'Happy Arabia,' known for its spices, incense, and the legendary kingdom of Sheba.

name: Arabia Petraea
description: Rocky region of Arabia, famous for the Nabatean city of Petra, carved into rose-red cliffs.

name: Asia
description: The Roman province of Asia, encompassing western Anatolia, where early Christian communities thrived.

name: Assyria
description: Ancient empire in Mesopotamia, known for its military prowess and the Biblical city of Nineveh.

name: Babylonia
description: Land of the Euphrates, home to Babylon, the Hanging Gardens, and the Biblical Tower of Babel.

name: Baetica
description: Roman province in southern Iberia, known for its olive oil, wine, and later, the Visigothic Kingdom.

name: Bythnia et Pontus
description: Northern Anatolia, where the apostle Peter addressed early Christians and Nicomedia became a key Roman city.

name: Caucasus
description: Mountainous region between the Black and Caspian Seas, a crossroads of cultures and ancient trade routes.

name: Cilicia
description: Southeastern Anatolia, birthplace of St.Paul and a hub for early Christian missionary journeys.

name: Creta
description: Island in the Mediterranean, known in antiquity for its Minoan civilization and mentioned in the New Testament.

name: Cyprus
description: Mediterranean island where St.Paul preached, and home to ancient city-kingdoms like Paphos and Salamis.

name: Cyrenaica
description: Eastern Libya, known for its Greek colonies and as the birthplace of the philosopher Eratosthenes.

name: Dalmatia
description: Coastal region of the eastern Adriatic, part of the Roman province of Illyricum and later medieval Croatia.

name: Epirus
description: Northwestern Greece, homeland of Pyrrhus and a region of rugged mountains and ancient oracle sites.

name: Galatia
description: Central Anatolia, where St.Paul wrote his Epistle to the Galatians, addressing early Christian communities.

name: Hispania
description: Roman name for the Iberian Peninsula, encompassing modern Spain and Portugal, rich in Roman and medieval history.

name: India
description: Ancient land of the Indus Valley, known for its spices, philosophy, and early trade with the Roman Empire.

name: Italia
description: Heart of the Roman Empire, home to Rome, the eternal city, and the center of early Christianity.

name: Judaea
description: Biblical heartland of the Jewish people, centered around Jerusalem and the Holy Land.

name: Lacus Asphaltites
description: The Dead Sea, a salt lake bordered by Israel and Jordan, known for its mineral-rich waters and Biblical significance.

name: Lycia et Pamphylia
description: Coastal regions of southern Anatolia, mentioned in the Acts of the Apostles as part of St.Paul's missionary journeys.

name: Macedonia
description: Northern Greece, homeland of Alexander the Great and a key region in the spread of early Christianity.

name: Mare Adriaticum
description: The Adriatic Sea, separating Italy from the Balkans, a historic maritime route for trade and exploration.

name: Mare Internum
description: The Mediterranean Sea, the 'middle of the earth,' cradle of ancient civilizations and a crossroads of trade.

name: Mare Rubrum
description: The Red Sea, a vital trade route linking the Mediterranean to the Indian Ocean, famous for the Biblical Exodus.

name: Parthia
description: Ancient empire in Persia, rival to Rome, known for its cavalry and the Silk Road trade routes.

name: Sabaea
description: Ancient kingdom in southern Arabia, famed for its wealth and the Queen of Sheba's visit to Solomon.

name: Sarmatia
description: Vast steppes north of the Black Sea, home to nomadic Sarmatian tribes and later part of the Eurasian trade network.

name: Sicilia
description: Largest island in the Mediterranean, a crossroads of Greek, Roman, and Norman cultures, and home to Mount Etna.

name: Syria
description: Ancient region of the Fertile Crescent, home to Damascus, one of the world's oldest continuously inhabited cities.

name: Syrtis
description: Coastal region of ancient Libya, known to the Greeks and Romans for its dangerous sands and harbours.

name: Thracia
description: Southeastern Europe, home to the Greek city of Byzantium (later Constantinople under the Romans and then Istanbul after the Ottoman conquest), a bridge between Europe and Asia.
